task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers answering what the below-market label means in Stoneharbor's new rental program. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Stoneharbor rental program caps the stated rent of participating homes at 80% of the program's annually published reference rent.
The reference is a program benchmark for a defined type of home, not a calculation based on each tenant's actual household income.
The program's illustration uses a $1,000 monthly reference rent, producing an $800 participating-home rent.
For a hypothetical household with $2,000 in gross monthly income, that $800 rent alone would equal 40% of its gross income.
The example is instructional and does not disclose a real tenant's income or establish the typical household burden.
Utilities and any separately listed service charges are not included in the simple reference-rent comparison.
The first program agreement covers 70 privately managed apartments, not all new rental housing in the city.
The apartments remain under the participating owners' management rather than becoming city-owned public housing.
Housing director Vera Dall said, "The label needs its number beside it. A reduction from a benchmark does not tell us what every household can manage."
Applicants must meet the program's published eligibility conditions, but the packet does not supply a universal income cutoff or a guarantee of an offer.
A housing advice group asked the city to show total expected housing charges, not only the discounted base rent, in its listings.
Advice worker Perrin Moss said, "People need the amount they will actually have to find each month, including the lines below the headline rent."
The participating agreements apply the rent restriction for five years, with any extension requiring a further agreement.
The city has not promised that every property will remain in the program indefinitely.
An annual benchmark revision can change the cap, but individual tenancy terms and notice arrangements must still be considered under the program documents.
The city plans to publish the benchmark source and the date it applies to so applicants can compare like periods.
The program does not give participants a right to buy their apartments as part of this rental agreement.
The advice group distinguishes this scheme from separate emergency accommodation and direct rent-assistance programs.
No occupancy results, average tenant incomes or citywide rent effect have yet been reported for the new agreement.
The 70 homes are spread across three existing buildings with different layouts and service-charge arrangements.
The city will check participating landlords' submitted rent schedules against the program cap.
The definition supplied is specific to this local program and does not establish a universal meaning of affordable housing.

forbidden_additions: Rent fixed at a percentage of each actual tenant's income.
The example treated as a typical household or a universal affordability test.
Permanent restrictions, city ownership or a right to purchase the homes.
preserve: Below a reference rent distinguished from affordable to a particular household.
The limits of the agreement, additional charges and illustrative arithmetic.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
